title: Power-Constrained Printed Neuromorphic Hardware Training
problem: Printed neuromorphic circuits (pNCs) must operate under severe power budgets from printed batteries or energy harvesters while maintaining task accuracy; traditional penalty-based optimization requires hundreds of training runs to explore power-accuracy tradeoffs.
motivation: Ultra-low-cost flexible printed electronics enable novel wearable/IoT applications but power budgets are orders of magnitude tighter than silicon; efficient training methods that generate Pareto-optimal solutions in single runs are critical.
method: Augmented Lagrangian optimization enforces task-specific power constraints directly during training, computing optimal power-accuracy tradeoffs in a single run. Tested across 13 benchmarks with different activation functions (p-tanh, p-Clipped_ReLU).
key_novelty: Augmented Lagrangian training approach that directly enforces power constraints and generates full Pareto front in single training run versus penalty-based methods requiring 150+ runs.
contributions: Augmented Lagrangian formulation for power-constraint enforcement in printed neuromorphic training
Achieves Pareto-optimal power-accuracy tradeoffs in single run versus 150 runs for penalty-based baseline
52-59x accuracy-to-power ratio improvement at low/high power budgets; 81.82% accuracy at high budgets with p-tanh activation

metrics.other: 52-59x accuracy-to-power improvement; 81.82% accuracy at high power

limitations: Evaluation limited to 13 benchmark datasets; applicability to large-scale neuromorphic systems not explored.
primary_theme: Augmented Lagrangian training for power-constrained printed neuromorphic circuits
